title: Semilocal G-rings are quasi-excellent
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian G-ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Assume that $A$ is semilocal, meaning that it has only finitely many maximal ideals. Then $A$ is J-2: for every finite type commutative $A$-algebra $D$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], the subset $\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}D:D_{\mathfrak p}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Thus $A$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Section 2, printed p.2, assertion that every semi-local G-ring is J-2, citing Matsumura, Commutative Algebra (1980), Theorem 76; used again immediately after (5.1) on printed p.9.

proof.text: If $A=0$, every unital $A$-algebra is zero, its spectrum is empty, and the desired open set is empty. Hence assume $A\ne0$ and enumerate its finitely many maximal ideals as $\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_r$, with $r\ge1$. Put $R_i=A_{\mathfrak m_i}$ and $C_i=\varprojlim_nR_i/(\mathfrak m_iR_i)^n$. The localization is a Noetherian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Its completion $C_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_iC_i$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and complete for that ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. Thus [lem-per-complete-local-excellence] makes $C_i$ excellent.

The map $A\to R_i$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular]. The map $R_i\to C_i$ is regular by the given G-ring condition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], applied to $\mathfrak m_i$. For each prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the fibre $C_i\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], since $C_i$ is Noetherian. These are all the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition], so the composite $A\to C_i$ is regular, in particular flat.

source.place: Tags 07GH (definition-G-ring), 07QI (lemma-regular-composition), and the localization observation in the proof of 07PT (lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals); fibre Noetherianity from Algebra 00E6 and 00FN.

proof.text: Set $B=\prod_{i=1}^r C_i$ with the diagonal map $A\to B$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules], applied to the flat $A$-modules of Step 2. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i$ the composite $B\to C_i\to\kappa(\mathfrak m_i)$ is a unital map onto a nonzero field, and kills $\mathfrak m_iB$, by the residue-field description in [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Hence $\mathfrak m_iB\ne B$. The list contains every maximal ideal of $A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] proves that $A\to B$ is faithfully flat.

Let $D$ be any finite type $A$-algebra and put $E_i=D\otimes_A C_i$, with structural map $D\to E_i$. The ring $D$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. If $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ generate $D$ over $A$, their elements $d_j\otimes1$ generate $E_i$ over $C_i$: expand the first entry of each pure tensor as a polynomial in the $d_j$, then absorb its scalar into the second entry. Thus $E_i$ is finite type over $C_i$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and Noetherian by the same Noetherianity lemma. Since $C_i$ is excellent, the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring] makes $\operatorname{Reg}(E_i)$ open. Also $D\to E_i$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change], using Step 2 and the finite type map $A\to D$; the tensor symmetry identifies its stated base change with this $E_i$.

Fix $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}E_i$ and let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap D$. The regular map $D\to E_i$ is flat by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] gives a flat local homomorphism $D_{\mathfrak p}\to(E_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings. If $(E_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] implies that $D_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local.

Conversely assume $D_{\mathfrak p}$ regular local, for the same $i,\mathfrak q,\mathfrak p$. Since $E_i$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] applied to $D\to E_i$ says the local homomorphism $D_{\mathfrak p}\to(E_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular. Its closed fibre is geometrically regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], hence regular (take the identity finite purely inseparable field extension). By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] that fibre is $(E_i)_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p(E_i)_{\mathfrak q}$: elements of $D_{\mathfrak p}$ outside its maximal ideal are units in the target because the map is local. The source and target are Noetherian local rings by Step 5, and the map is flat. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] implies that $(E_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local. Together with Step 5, this proves that the inverse image of $\operatorname{Reg}(D)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}E_i$ is exactly $\operatorname{Reg}(E_i)$.

source.place: More on Algebra Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local); Algebra Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre); the fibre formula in More on Algebra Tag 07BZ (definition-regular).

proof.text: Put $E=D\otimes_A B$. The component projections give an isomorphism $E\cong\prod_iE_i$. Explicitly its inverse sends a tuple of pure tensors in component $i$ to the sum of their tensors with the $C_i$ entry embedded into $B$ in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere; additivity and the balanced relation show this is well-defined, and both composites are identities by the coordinate idempotents. In a finite product each prime selects exactly one component: among the orthogonal coordinate idempotents $e_i$ summing to $1$, exactly one is outside the prime. On the open-and-closed subset $D(e_i)$ the product's localization is $E_i$, by projection and extension in coordinate $i$. Basic opens restrict to the corresponding basic opens in that component, so $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is the disjoint union of the $\operatorname{Spec}E_i$ and its local rings there are the component local rings. Steps 4–6 now say that the inverse image of $\operatorname{Reg}(D)$ under $g:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a union of opens in these open-and-closed components, and is therefore open.

source.place: Elementary finite-product idempotent and balanced-tensor calculations; Algebra Section 00DY, basic opens of the prime spectrum.

proof.text: The map $D\to E=D\otimes_A B$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], applied to Step 3. Thus $g$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. It is quasi-compact: for each basic open $D(d)\subset\operatorname{Spec}D$ its inverse image is $D(d\otimes1)=\operatorname{Spec}E_{d\otimes1}$, which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; any quasi-compact open in the target is a finite union of basic opens, by choosing a finite subcover from its basis cover. We may therefore apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map]. Step 7 gives the open inverse image required by this quotient-topology statement, so $\operatorname{Reg}(D)$ is open.

The algebra $D$ in Step 4 was arbitrary, so Step 8 proves the stated J-2 condition. Since $A$ is already Noetherian and a G-ring, the definition [def-exc-excellent-ring] now says precisely that $A$ is quasi-excellent. In the zero-ring case of Step 1 the same definition applies, because the J-2 quantification has only zero algebras.
